clue.text: Your status before fertilizer made you? No more than a blinking insert in the old man's magazine!

definitions.text: Your status before fertilizer made you? No more than a blinking insert in the old man's magazine!

parts.words: Your status before fertilizer made you
parts.note: a cryptic picture of the time before conception, when the 'fertilizer' is the sperm that made you

parts.words: No more than a blinking insert in the old man's magazine
parts.note: a blink is a twinkle, the insert is a sperm and the old man's magazine is his store of it, a crude take on the eye

explanation.walkthrough: The setter bends the familiar phrase about not yet being born into a smutty joke: 'blinking' gives the twinkle, 'insert' and 'magazine' turn the eye into something lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone not yet conceived, existing only as a hope or intention in a parent's mind.

clue.text: Antihero Clive on his beach, getting end away

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Clive James, the Australian broadcaster and critic

indicators.note: the beach name loses its final letter; also slang for having sex, which suits the subject

parts.note: Bondi is the famous Sydney beach, his as Clive James is Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian TV critic enjoys a sexual conquest on his home beach in Sydney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting one's end away' is British slang for having sex, which suits a womanising spy and doubles as the instruction to drop the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleming's ruthless, womanising spy is often described as a flawed antihero rather than a conventional moral champion.

clue.text: Cap'n Bob? Not one to give you the full story

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Private Eye's nickname for Robert Maxwell, who sailed his yacht and so was a ship's captain

definitions.text: Not one to give you the full story
definitions.meaning: second meaning: someone who skips parts, leaving bits out

explanation.walkthrough: Robert Maxwell, the newspaper owner, was mocked by Private Eye as Cap'n Bob; the second half also nods at his creative accounting.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat's captain is a skipper, and a reader or teller who jumps over passages is also one.

clue.text: See you make TV reporter socially acceptable

parts.note: Kate Adie, the BBC's long-serving war correspondent
U means upper-class, proper, as in the old 'U and non-U' usage

explanation.surface: A plea to make a television journalist respectable enough for polite society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See you' looks like part of the instruction but is the farewell being defined.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye, the French farewell being used in English as well.

clue.text: Piss-artist — and plonker?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for a heavy drinker
second meaning, made up for the clue: one who drinks plonk, cheap wine; normally plonker means a fool

explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is everyday British slang for an idiot, but here it is read as someone who downs plonk, which is cheap wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A habitual drinker of cheap alcohol, the classic street drunk, fits both the slang insult and the invented sense.

clue.text: Gore rents out with complete absence of self-reproach

indicators.note: letters that are out are put out of place, so the two words are rearranged

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A politician called Gore lets out his properties and feels no guilt about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Having nothing at all to be sorry about means feeling no remorse for anything done.

clue.text: Member not so much following as pissed

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first in the answer

parts.note: a limb, here a leg
a smaller amount, i.e. less

explanation.surface: Someone becoming less of a follower as they get drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Pissed is British slang for drunk, not angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being so drunk you cannot stand up is a common British slang expression for heavy intoxication.

clue.text: One who's thick with ex-dictator getting round Thatcher initially

parts.note: Idi Amin, the deposed Ugandan dictator
a round shape, the letter O

indicators.note: take only the opening letter of the word Thatcher

parts.note: the former prime minister's name supplies its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone who is close friends with a former tyrant, cosying up to Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thick with' suggests being friendly with someone, but thick is the definition, meaning stupid.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick person is a stupid one, and this is the commonest word for a fool.

clue.text: Object to Amin gruesomely going round knocking off both men and women

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the short piece
the dictator's name and the short word are mangled gruesomely into a new order

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be jumbled

parts.words: knocking off both men and women
parts.note: having sex with either sex, i.e. bisexual, abbreviated BI

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the dictator's horrid promiscuous behaviour with men and women alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object to' reads as a verb, but 'to' belongs with the name in the jumble and Object is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal one strives towards is an object, as in 'the object of the exercise'.

clue.text: "One has to interrupt reign, sadly, and get back"

indicators.note: the single letter breaks into the middle of the jumbled word
the word reign is treated badly and its letters reordered

parts.note: the word itself supplies the letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A deposed monarch who must sadly break off from ruling, hoping to return.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover something lost, such as the throne, is to obtain it once more.

clue.text: Bellow about flipping part-time visionary

indicators.note: the novelist's first name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Saul Bellow, the American novelist

indicators.note: the abbreviation is turned over so its letters run the other way

parts.note: PT is the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Someone shouting about an annoying fantasist who only dreams some of the time.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellow looks like a verb, but it is the novelist; fittingly, the apostle was called Saul before his conversion.
explanation.definitionFit: The apostle had a vision of Christ on the road to Damascus, making him a famous seer of revelations.

clue.text: Allow rotten toe-rag Livingstone finally inside

indicators.note: that letter is placed within the rearranged word
the six letters are in a bad state and must be reordered

parts.note: British slang for a contemptible person

indicators.note: only the closing letter of Livingstone is used

parts.note: Ken Livingstone, then Mayor of London; his surname supplies its last letter

explanation.surface: Letting a nasty layabout into the house, with Ken Livingstone (then London's mayor) shut in too.
explanation.walkthrough: A toe-rag is British slang for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent to something is to permit it, so the phrasal verb works as a synonym.

clue.text: Seat that's been dumped

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a piece of excrement, from 'having a dump'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dumped' sounds like being jilted; it is crude slang for defecating.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a simple backless seat and, medically, a lump of faeces.

clue.text: See 1
See 1
Member of society complimentary to Brenda and Brian, relatively speaking

parts.note: given without charge, free
Private Eye's name for the Queen, mother of Charles
Private Eye's name for Prince Charles, the Queen's son

explanation.surface: A courtier who flatters the Queen and Prince Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively speaking' tells you to read the royal pair by family relation: to Brian she is his mother, to Brenda he is her son.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masons are a secretive fraternal society, so one of its brethren is a member of it.

clue.text: Inclined to be gutless, like old newspaper that's had too much exposure?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: somewhat yellow, i.e. a little cowardly

definitions.text: like old newspaper that's had too much exposure
definitions.meaning: second meaning: newsprint turns a pale yellow in sunlight

explanation.walkthrough: Yellow means cowardly, and the -ish ending gives 'inclined to be'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tending towards a pale yellow tint describes both mild cowardice and newsprint left in the sun.

clue.text: Like Robin Cook, no minor personalities hiding euro fiasco

indicators.note: the grown-ups enclose the jumbled letters

parts.note: people who are not minors are grown-ups

indicators.note: the currency name is made a mess of, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: the currency's name supplies the letters to be scrambled

explanation.surface: The Foreign Secretary, no small figure, covering up a fiasco over the single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Cook, Labour's Foreign Secretary, left his wife in 1997 after his affair with his secretary was exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: The politician was unfaithful to his wife, the core meaning of conduct involving extramarital sex.

clue.text: Garland after learning to be a siren

indicators.note: the wreath comes after the learning

parts.note: knowledge passed down, lore
a Hawaiian flower wreath

explanation.surface: A singer like Judy Garland who studies hard to become a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: Garland suggests Judy Garland; it is the flower wreath.
explanation.definitionFit: In German legend she sang from a Rhine rock and lured boatmen to their deaths, a classic temptress.

clue.text: 'Horizontal kinetics' covers intercourse

indicators.note: the phrase's letters cover the answer, which lies inside them across the word break

parts.note: the answer sits in the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A smutty euphemism for sex being lying-down movement.
explanation.walkthrough: Intercourse here is conversation, not sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Intercourse has the older meaning of communication or dealings between people, which is spoken conversation.

clue.text: For women who want to avoid the issue of sex? Yes and no

definitions.text: For women who want to avoid the issue of sex? Yes and no

parts.words: For women who want to avoid the issue of sex
parts.note: reads as dodging the topic, but issue means offspring
yes to sex, no to children

explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoid the issue of sex' seems to mean not discussing it; the women want sex but not its issue, a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: The oral contraceptive prevents pregnancy while allowing sex, which is exactly the yes and no.

clue.text: The chief perversion of Euro MPs

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are perverted, twisted into a new arrangement

parts.note: the two words supply the letters to be twisted

explanation.surface: The boss of Strasbourg's sleaze: the worst vice of the European parliamentarians.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the overall boss or leader of an organisation, so the head person.

clue.text: Number less than ten, but superior to one African rebel movement

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: the units are the single digits below ten

explanation.surface: A rebel group in Africa that is small in number but rated above another.
explanation.walkthrough: UNITA was the Angolan rebel army led by Jonas Savimbi.
explanation.definitionFit: It was the anti-government guerrilla organisation in Angola's long civil war.

clue.text: In the fashion of one detested by Thatcher — nothing but a product of apartheid

parts.note: in this manner, so
Thatcher scorned moderate Tories in her cabinet as wets

explanation.surface: Something done in the style of Thatcher's enemies is nothing but apartheid's legacy.
explanation.walkthrough: Wets were the moderate Conservatives Thatcher disdained.
explanation.definitionFit: The Johannesburg township was built under apartheid to house Black workers away from white areas.

clue.text: Talk means sod all to a shit, note

parts.note: British slang for nothing, a zero
a nasty person, a rat
a musical note

explanation.surface: Speech counts for nothing to a nasty man, take note.
explanation.walkthrough: Sod all is British slang for nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak at length, often pompously, is to hold forth with a speech.

clue.text: Reportedly talented but topped by Caine soundly

definitions.note: said aloud, Caine is Cain, who murdered his brother; topped is slang for killed

indicators.note: the word for talented is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: talented means able, and the answer is pronounced the same as that word

explanation.surface: Michael Caine is said to be a gifted actor, and someone else was beaten by him.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves work by sound: the brother's name is heard as 'able', and the actor's surname is heard as the biblical murderer. Topped is British slang for killed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, the shepherd son of Adam and Eve was murdered by his elder brother out of jealousy.

clue.text: Magazines, etc, like Punch ­ bust without the foreign intervention

indicators.note: in the old sense of outside, so the breasts surround the article
the French article comes between the letters of the other word

parts.note: slang for breasts
LE is French for the

explanation.surface: A satirical magazine taking a swipe at a bust without foreign interference.
explanation.walkthrough: Punch was the long-running British humour magazine; 'without' means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Publications are referred to by publishers as their titles, and Punch was one of the best known.

clue.text: City supporters — one has trouble on the way back

parts.note: bras support breasts

indicators.note: the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell or in difficulty

explanation.surface: Football fans of a team called City, one of whom gets into bother travelling home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City supporters' reads as football fans; City is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the planned capital city of Brazil, built in the 1950s.

clue.text: Perhaps Scottish or Welsh constitution is a major concern of Blair and co, currently

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the physical constitution, or health, of a nation such as Scotland or Wales

definitions.text: a major concern of Blair and co, currently
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the NHS, which Blair's government was then pledging to fix

explanation.walkthrough: Constitution suggests the devolution settlements of 1999; it means bodily health. The NHS is Britain's state health service.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is short for the National Health Service and can also mean a country's state of wellbeing.
